docs.title: PMI Analyzer (شامخ)
docs.text: Welcome to the PMI Analyzer documentation!

docs.title: What is PMI Analyzer?
docs.text:
PMI Analyzer is a Python package for automatic analysis of Iran's Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), known as Shamkh (شامخ).

It provides:

  • PDF Parsing: Extract PMI data from ICCIMA PDF reports
  • Data Analysis: Calculate trends, composites, and rolling means
  • Visualization: Generate interactive charts
  • Export: Save data to CSV, SQL, JSON, or Excel

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from pmi_analyzer.parser.pdf_parser import PDFParser
from pmi_analyzer.metrics.calculator import MetricsCalculator

# Parse a PMI PDF report
parser = PDFParser()
results = parser.parse(Path("data/pdfs/report.pdf"))

# Access the metrics
metrics = results[0]
print(f"PMI Total: {metrics.pmi_total}")
print(f"Production: {metrics.production}")

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install pmi-analyzer

For Excel export support:

pip install pmi-analyzer[excel]

docs.title: What is Shamkh?
docs.text: Shamkh (شامخ) is Iran's official Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), published monthly by the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture (ICCIMA).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Launched: 2019
  • Publisher: ICCIMA (ایکاما)
  • Frequency: Monthly
  • Format: PDF reports in Persian

docs.title: How Shamkh is Calculated
docs.text: Shamkh is a weighted average of 11 sub-indicators:

docs.title: Core Indicators (70%)
docs.text: Indicator Persian Weight Production تولید 20% New Orders سفارشات جدید 20% Sales فروش 15% Raw Materials Inventory موجودی مواد اولیه 5% Final Goods Inventory موجودی محصول نهایی 5% Input Price قیمت مواد اولیه 5% Production Expectations انتظارات تولید 5%

docs.title: Extended Indicators (30%)
docs.text: Indicator Persian Weight Employment استخدام 10% Exports صادرات 10% Delivery Speed سرعت تحویل 5% Business Activity فعالیت اقتصادی 5%

docs.title: Interpreting Shamkh
docs.text: Shamkh Value Economic Condition > 55 Strong Expansion 50 - 55 Moderate Expansion 45 - 50 Mild Contraction < 45 Severe Contraction

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
• PDF Reports: Available at iccima.ir
  • Archive: Historical reports on otaghiranonline.ir

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
1. Survey-based: Subject to respondent bias
  2. Manufacturing-focused: Primarily covers industrial sector
  3. Lagging release: Reports published 1-2 months after reference period
  4. Language barrier: Reports in Persian only

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Iran's Shamkh includes 11 sub-indicators, each measured on a 0-100 scale.

docs.title: Production (تولید)
docs.text:
Measures manufacturing output volume.

  • > 50: Production is increasing
  • < 50: Production is decreasing

docs.title: New Orders (سفارشات جدید)
docs.text:
Measures new customer orders received.

  • > 50: Demand is growing
  • < 50: Demand is shrinking

docs.title: Sales (فروش)
docs.text:
Measures product sales volume.

  • > 50: Sales are increasing
  • < 50: Sales are decreasing

docs.title: Raw Materials Inventory (موجودی مواد اولیه)
docs.text:
Measures raw material stock levels.

  • > 50: Inventory is building up
  • < 50: Inventory is being depleted

docs.title: Final Goods Inventory (موجودی محصول نهایی)
docs.text:
Measures finished goods stock levels.

  • > 50: Finished goods accumulating
  • < 50: Finished goods being shipped

docs.title: Input Price (قیمت مواد اولیه)
docs.text:
Measures purchase prices of raw materials.

  • > 50: Prices are rising (inflationary)
  • < 50: Prices are falling (deflationary)

docs.title: Production Expectations (انتظارات تولید)
docs.text:
Measures expected production volume next month.

  • > 50: Optimistic outlook
  • < 50: Pessimistic outlook

docs.title: Employment (استخدام)
docs.text:
Measures hiring activity.

  • > 50: Companies are hiring
  • < 50: Companies are laying off

docs.title: Exports (صادرات)
docs.text:
Measures export volume.

  • > 50: Exports are increasing
  • < 50: Exports are decreasing

docs.title: Delivery Speed (سرعت تحویل)
docs.text:
Measures supplier delivery times.

  • > 50: Deliveries are faster
  • < 50: Deliveries are slower

docs.title: Business Activity (فعالیت اقتصادی)
docs.text:
Measures overall business activity.

  • > 50: Business is expanding
  • < 50: Business is contracting

docs.title: The Purchasing Managers' Index
docs.text: The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) is a key economic indicator derived from monthly surveys of private sector companies. It measures the health of the manufacturing and service sectors.

docs.title: How PMI Works
docs.text:
PMI is calculated from five sub-indicators, each weighted equally (20%):

Indicator Weight What it Measures New Orders 20% Future demand Production 20% Current output Employment 20% Hiring activity Supplier Delivery Times 20% Supply chain speed Stock of Items Purchased 20% Inventory levels

docs.title: Interpreting PMI Values
docs.text:
Value Meaning > 50 Expansion - Economy is growing = 50 Neutral - No change < 50 Contraction - Economy is shrinking

The further from 50, the stronger the trend:

  • PMI = 55.0 → Strong expansion
  • PMI = 50.0 → No change
  • PMI = 45.0 → Moderate contraction

docs.title: Why PMI Matters
docs.text:
1. Leading Indicator: PMI is released before most other economic data
  2. Monthly Frequency: Provides timely economic insights
  3. Sector Coverage: Covers manufacturing and services
  4. Global Standard: Used worldwide for economic analysis

docs.title: PMI in Iran: Shamkh
docs.text:
Iran's PMI is called Shamkh (شامخ), published by the Iran Chamber of Commerce (ICCIMA) since 2019.

For more details, see Shamkh Explained.

docs.title: analyse
docs.text:
Analyze Shamkh (PMI) data from a PDF file.

pmi-analyzer analyse [OPTIONS]

Options:

Option Description --download Download latest report from iccima.ir --pdf PATH Path to local PDF file --output PATH Output directory (default: output) --historical-csv PATH Path to historical CSV --plot Generate full sub-indicators chart --composite Generate composite indicators chart --inventory Generate inventory comparison chart --expectations Generate production expectations chart --labor Generate employment & exports chart

Examples:

# Analyze a local PDF
pmi-analyzer analyse --pdf data/pdfs/report.pdf

# Download and analyze latest
pmi-analyzer analyse --download

# Generate all charts
pmi-analyzer analyse --pdf report.pdf --plot --composite --inventory

# Export with historical data
pmi-analyzer analyse --pdf report.pdf --historical-csv data/shamkh_historical.csv

docs.title: build-historical
docs.text:
Build historical Shamkh database from scratch.

pmi-analyzer build-historical [OPTIONS]

Options:

Option Description --csv PATH Output CSV path --pdf-dir PATH Directory for downloaded PDFs --delay FLOAT Delay between requests (seconds) --verbose Show debug logs

Example:

# Build full historical database
pmi-analyzer build-historical --csv data/shamkh_historical.csv --verbose

docs.title: Parse a PDF Report
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from pmi_analyzer.parser.pdf_parser import PDFParser

# Initialize parser
parser = PDFParser()

# Parse a PMI PDF report
results = parser.parse(Path("data/pdfs/shamkh_khordad_1405.pdf"))

# Access the metrics
metrics = results[0]
print(f"Month: {metrics.month}")
print(f"PMI Total: {metrics.pmi_total}")
print(f"Production: {metrics.production}")
print(f"New Orders: {metrics.new_orders}")

docs.title: Export to Different Formats
docs.text:
from pmi_analyzer.data.exporter import (
    export_to_csv,
    export_to_sql,
    export_to_json,
    export_to_excel,
)

# Export to CSV
export_to_csv(results, Path("output/pmi_data.csv"))

# Export to SQL
export_to_sql(results, Path("output/pmi_data.sql"), table_name="pmi_data")

# Export to JSON
export_to_json(results, Path("output/pmi_data.json"))

# Export to Excel (requires openpyxl)
export_to_excel(results, Path("output/pmi_data.xlsx"))

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: PMI Analyzer supports exporting data to 4 formats: CSV, SQL, JSON, and Excel.

docs.title: CSV Export
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from pmi_analyzer.data.exporter import export_to_csv

export_to_csv(results, Path("output/pmi_data.csv"))

Features: - UTF-8 with BOM for Excel compatibility - All indicators as columns - NaN values preserved

docs.title: SQL Export
docs.text:
from pmi_analyzer.data.exporter import export_to_sql

export_to_sql(
    results,
    Path("output/pmi_data.sql"),
    table_name="pmi_data"
)

Features: - CREATE TABLE statement included - INSERT statements for each row - NULL handling for missing values - Single-quote escaping

docs.title: JSON Export
docs.text:
from pmi_analyzer.data.exporter import export_to_json

export_to_json(results, Path("output/pmi_data.json"))

Features: - JSON array format - Unicode preserved (no escaping) - Configurable indentation - null for missing values

docs.title: Excel Export
docs.text:
from pmi_analyzer.data.exporter import export_to_excel

export_to_excel(
    results,
    Path("output/pmi_data.xlsx"),
    sheet_name="PMI Data"
)

Requirements: 

pip install openpyxl

docs.title: Including Calculated Metrics
docs.text:
All export functions accept include_calculated=True:

export_to_csv(
    results,
    Path("output/pmi_data.csv"),
    include_calculated=True  # Includes trends, composites, rolling means
)

docs.title: Merging with Historical Data
docs.text:
from pmi_analyzer.data.exporter import merge_with_historical

# Merge new data with existing CSV
df = merge_with_historical(
    results,
    Path("data/shamkh_historical.csv")
)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The PDF parser extracts PMI data from ICCIMA PDF reports using multiple strategies.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from pathlib import Path
from pmi_analyzer.parser.pdf_parser import PDFParser

parser = PDFParser()
results = parser.parse(Path("data/pdfs/shamkh_khordad_1405.pdf"))

metrics = results[0]
print(f"Month: {metrics.month}")
print(f"PMI Total: {metrics.pmi_total}")

docs.title: Extraction Strategies
docs.text:
The parser tries multiple strategies in order:

  1. Table Extraction: Structured table parsing via pdfplumber
  2. Spatial Clustering: Word-coordinate based extraction
  3. Chart Labels: Matches indicator words to nearby numbers
  4. Text Fallback: Regex-based plain text extraction

docs.title: Handling RTL Text
docs.text:
The parser handles Persian Right-to-Left text:

# Labels can be in standard or reversed format
label = "شاخص کل اقتصاد"  # Standard
label_reversed = "داصتقا لک خماش"  # Reversed (from PDF)

docs.title: Cross-Tab Tables
docs.text:
The parser detects and handles industry breakdown tables:

# Automatically prefers aggregate rows over industry-specific rows
parser = PDFParser()
results = parser.parse(pdf_path)  # Extracts main PMI, not industry breakdown

docs.title: Month Detection
docs.text:
Automatic month detection from PDF text:

parser = PDFParser()
results = parser.parse(pdf_path)
print(results[0].month)  # e.g., "1405-03"

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
from pmi_analyzer.exceptions import ParseError

parser = PDFParser()
try:
    results = parser.parse(Path("report.pdf"))
except ParseError as e:
    print(f"Parsing failed: {e}")
